digest.component_or_area: Review gates (plan review and code review)
propositions: Plan review and code review currently make independent discovery decisions through partially independent registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths, causing policy ownership defects where one review gate can disable built-ins, omit criteria, ignore applicability, or mistake failed work for success.

Implement a unified discovery architecture where both gates derive selection from one immutable effective-policy snapshot containing built-ins, project LLM criteria, project DET criteria, routing, prompts, posture, and applicability, with a shared executor owning typed outcomes, usage, budget enforcement, and success-only checkpoint mechanics.

Project code-review LLM criteria must require non-empty repository-relative globs (migrate `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]`); positive explicit `usd_budget` values are authoritative on both gates; for code review omission is uncapped, for plan review omission preserves existing budget policy.

Add `rebar review-plan --retry` to retry only the literal latest completed INDETERMINATE review with retryable missing calls, reusing content-identical successes and granting each explicit retry a fresh attempt budget, documented across all canonical CLI surfaces.

Plan review must move to digest-complete success-only checkpoint namespace (legacy checkpoints never seed new path) while preserving chunking, concurrency, cache warming, and cancellation behavior; code review preserves sequential execution, no checkpoints, and authored YAML/BPMN topology.
The workflow editor must show editable Authored Workflow separately from read-only Effective Policy and reject empty project code-review LLM glob lists.
